question: What are the methods by which LLMs reason in continuous hidden states rather than in verbalised chain-of-thought tokens, and how do they fit together?
hypothesis: Moving reasoning from discrete tokens into continuous hidden states raises expressive bandwidth and the performance ceiling of reasoning.
contributions: A unified formulation of latent CoT over spatial (layer) and temporal (hidden-state) updates
A taxonomy: vertical (activation-based) recurrence vs horizontal (hidden-state) recurrence, plus fine-tuning strategies that compress or internalise explicit traces
A mechanistic-interpretability section on layers as the substrate of latent reasoning
A discussion of infinite-depth reasoning via text diffusion models and optimisation-over-time views

results.claim: Explicit CoT tokens carry about 15 bits each while a 2560-dim FP16 hidden state carries about 40,960 bits, a roughly 2.7e3-fold bandwidth gap.
results.setup: Figure 1 illustration; arithmetic on one hidden-state width (2560) and FP16.
results.quote: Explicit reasoning transmits discrete tokens (≈15 bits each), whereas latent reasoning exchanges full 2560-dimensional FP16 hidden states (≈40, 960 bits each), revealing a ∼2.7 × 103- fold bandwidth gap between the two approaches.

results.claim: CODI, using single-step self-distillation alignment of hidden states, is described as the first latent method to match explicit CoT on GSM8K.
results.setup: Reported from Shen et al. (CODI); training-induced recurrence.
results.quote: achieving parity with explicit CoT on GSM8K for the first time among latent methods

results.claim: System-1.5 Reasoning is reported as over 20x faster inference on GSM8K while preserving chain-of-thought accuracy.
results.setup: Reported from [109]; GSM8K; no backbone modification.
results.quote: delivering over 20× faster inference on GSM8K while preserving chain-of-thought accuracy

results.quote: even meaningless filler tokens (e.g., "......") can improve reasoning by simply providing more attention steps

results.quote: any K-layer transformer performing m-step CoT reasoning can be simulated by an (L+O(1)) layer transformer through m iterative forward passes

results.claim: At least 2-3 layers are needed to form a complete two-step reasoning chain inside the model.
results.quote: at least 2-3 layers are required to form a complete two-step reasoning chain within the model

limits: No empirical comparison across latent methods: models are trained under disparate conditions and mostly compared to non-reasoning LLM baselines (Section 6).
Authors concede hidden-state methods (linear/gradient-state) have not yet shown enhanced reasoning (3.2.2).
Latent states are not human-readable, so interpretability and training are harder than explicit CoT (2.2).
Almost all numbers are reported from other papers; the survey runs no experiments.
Infini-attention is flagged as unreliable by a reproduction (5.2.1).
Preprint v2 dated 10 Jul 2025; the field moves fast.
It says nothing about prompting reasoning models; latent CoT here is an architecture/training topic.
practices: Prefer a modular Pre/Loop/Coda recurrent design with simple stopping (fixed iterations or early exit); depth embeddings and complex ACT have been dropped (3.1.1).
Use curriculum training that gradually removes explicit CoT tokens when internalising reasoning (Stepwise Internalization, Coconut) (3.1.4).
Align recurrence steps with reasoning steps, e.g. RELAY loss L = L_ans + lambda L_iter (3.1.4).
Use progressive stacking (MIDAS) to stabilise loop-model training (3.1.4).
Use chunk-wise parallelisation for gradient-state recurrence: parallel within chunks, recurrent across chunks (3.2.2).
Convert pretrained Transformers to recurrent students by distillation rather than training from scratch (3.2.3).
Treat Infini-attention with caution; rope scaling or Ring Attention are more viable (5.2.1).

terms.definition: Latent Chain-of-Thought carries reasoning in continuous internal representations, often via recurrent mechanisms within the model, instead of discrete tokens.
Activation-based methods that apply feedback loops to activation values to expand computational depth.
Hidden-state-based methods that use hidden states to propagate context across long sequences of reasoning, increasing sequential capacity.
Three-stage recurrent design separating input encoding (Prelude), iterative reasoning (Loop blocks) and output decoding (Coda).
The last-layer hidden state of the previous step, fed back as the next input position (Coconut).
Treating the hidden state as online-learning parameters updated by an optimisation step: S_t = alpha_t S_{t-1} - eta_t grad l(S_{t-1}; k_t, v_t).
Individual layers specialise to distinct reasoning operations, forming an implicit computational pipeline analogous to explicit CoT.
An AI's ability to devote unbounded thinking time to refine a solution irrespective of output length.
Reasoning realised by diffusion models that iteratively denoise the whole output in parallel with bidirectional context.
